question: Does our existing calibrated whole-CNS LIF engine, untuned, reproduce the published connectome prediction that tonic DNg100 activation drives rhythmic front-leg motor neuron activity through the E1/E2 core interneurons?

reference.citation: Pugliese, Tuthill, Brunton et al. 2025, 'Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator circuit for fly walking', bioRxiv 10.1101/2025.09.12.675944 (preprint, not peer reviewed)
predictions_used: Left DNg100 tonic activation drives rhythmic activity in several front-leg motor neurons (motor rhythmicity score > 0.5 as their threshold).
Oscillation roughly matches real stepping frequency (~7-15 Hz).
DNg100 is among the highest-scoring excitatory descending neurons.
Silencing E1 (IN17A001) or E2 (INXXX466) abolishes the rhythm.
Higher DNg100 drive raises oscillation frequency.
reference.their_model: rate model of an isolated MANC front-leg network with randomly sampled cell parameters; they also report rhythmic spiking for the core circuit in an LIF model

feasibility_inspection_before_registrati: Confirmed presence only: DNg100 (2, L/R), IN17A001/INXXX466/IN16B036 (6 each), 931 acetylcholine descending neurons; engine step cost ~1.6 ms per 0.5 ms step. No stimulation run was performed.

engine.module: malecns_backend.neural.MaleCNSBrain with ModelConfig.calibrated(); no parameter changed
engine.data: malecns_backend.cache.load_cache over the canonical sources (fingerprints verified by load_cache)
engine.network: whole CNS as loaded; not a front-leg sub-network

readout.motor_neurons: union of dense indices of bodymap.json muscles entries whose name ends ' T1 left'
readout.binning: spike counts per 1 ms bin, Gaussian smoothing sigma 5 ms, converted to Hz
readout.active_mn: at least 5 spikes inside the analysis window
readout.rhythmicity_score: preprint method: trace scaled to [-1,1]; autocorrelation over positive lags; peaks with prominence >= 0.05; raw = min(max peak height, max peak prominence); period = lag of the most prominent peak; normalized by the same score of a frequency-matched sinusoid of equal duration, clipped to [0,1]; active MN without a qualifying peak scores 0
readout.simulation_score: mean over active MNs; NaN (infeasible) if no active MN
readout.condition_score: mean of feasible seeds; NaN if none feasible
readout.frequency: 1000/period_ms of each active MN with score > 0; simulation frequency = median; condition frequency = median over seeds

best_rate_rule: for DNg100 and each control neuron the condition score is the maximum over the four rates (mirrors the preprint's per-neuron input adjustment)

controls.descending_controls: 20 acetylcholine descending neurons other than DNg100, sampled without replacement by numpy default_rng(20261101) from the sorted dense-index list; 4 rates x seeds 1..4 each

necessity.copy_selection: for each of IN17A001 (E1) and INXXX466 (E2), the instance with the most total synapses onto the front-left MN set
necessity.intervention: transmission_withheld_indices = [selected copy] (it integrates and spikes, but its events are not delivered)
necessity.conditions: DNg100 at its best rate, seeds 1..16, E1 silenced and E2 silenced separately

acceptance.C1_rhythm: DNg100 best-rate score >= 0.5 AND greater than the 80th percentile of the feasible control best-rate scores
acceptance.C2_frequency: DNg100 frequency at its best rate within [5, 20] Hz
acceptance.C3_necessity: score < 0.5 with E1 silenced AND score < 0.5 with E2 silenced
acceptance.C4_drive_scaling_secondary: Spearman correlation of rate vs frequency over feasible DNg100 rates > 0 (reported; not part of the verdict)
acceptance.PARTIAL: C1 holds and C2 or C3 fails
acceptance.INCONCLUSIVE: engine/data hash mismatch, or DNg100 infeasible at all rates

interpretation_limits: Motor neuron spiking only; no body, physics or behavior.

Different from the preprint: whole-CNS spiking engine with fixed calibrated parameters, not an isolated rate network with sampled parameters. A mismatch may reflect that difference rather than either model being wrong.
A reproduction supports our engine's VNC dynamics for this pathway; it does not establish walking, coxa mappings or inter-leg coordination.
single_run: Executed once after protocol, code and tests are committed; no retries, rates, thresholds or windows changed after seeing results.
